Busan was once a center of military affairs in the southern region of the peninsula and therefore was an important site for diplomatic relationships with Japan; high-ranking officers and officials from the court frequently visited the city. Special foods were prepared for the officers such as *Dongnae pajeon* (동래파전), a variant of *[pajeon](/wiki/Pajeon "Pajeon")* (Korean savory pancakes), made with whole scallions, sliced chili peppers, and various kinds of seafood in a thick [batter](/wiki/Batter_(cooking) "Batter (cooking)") of wheat flour, glutinous rice flour, eggs, salt and water.[[61]](#cite_note-63)

During the Korean War, Busan was the biggest refugee destination on the peninsula; people from all regions of Korea went there. Some of these refugees stayed and adapted the recipes of their local specialties. One of these foods is *[milmyeon](/wiki/Milmyeon "Milmyeon")* (밀면) (lit. 'wheat noodle') a version of *[naengmyeon](/wiki/Naengmyeon "Naengmyeon")*, cold buckwheat noodle soup, but using wheat flour instead. The **history of mobile phones** covers mobile communication devices that connect wirelessly to the public switched telephone network.

UnitedHealth Group originated in late 1974, when Minnesota-based Charter Med Incorporated was founded by [Richard Taylor Burke](/wiki/Richard_T._Burke "Richard T. Burke"). It originally processed claims for doctors at the Hennepin County Medical Society.[[15]](#cite_note-15) UnitedHealthcare Corporation was founded in 1977 to purchase Charter Med and create a network-based health plan for seniors.[[16]](#cite_note-16) It became a publicly traded company in 1984 and changed its name to UnitedHealth Group in 1998.[[17]](#cite_note-17)

In 1988, UnitedHealthcare started its first [pharmacy benefit management](/wiki/Pharmacy_benefit_manager "Pharmacy benefit manager"), through its [Diversified Pharmaceutical Services](/wiki/Diversified_Pharmaceutical_Services "Diversified Pharmaceutical Services") subsidiary. It managed pharmacy benefits delivered both through retail pharmacies and mail. The subsidiary was sold to [SmithKline Beecham](/wiki/SmithKline_Beecham "SmithKline Beecham") in 1994 for $2.3 billion.[[18]](#cite_note-18)

In 1994, UnitedHealthcare acquired Ramsey-HMO, a Florida insurer.[[19]](#cite_note-19) In 1995, the company acquired The MetraHealth Companies Inc. for $1.65 billion. MetraHealth was a privately held company formed by combining the group healthcare operations of [The Travelers Companies](/wiki/The_Travelers_Companies "The Travelers Companies") and [MetLife](/wiki/MetLife "MetLife"). In 1996, UnitedHealthcare acquired HealthWise of America, which operated HMOs in Arkansas, Maryland, Kentucky and Tennessee.[[20]](#cite_note-20)

In 1998, the company was reorganized as the [holding company](/wiki/Holding_company "Holding company") for hitherto independent companies UnitedHealthcare, Ovations, Uniprise, Specialized Care Services, and Ingenix and rebranded as "UnitedHealth Group". Also in 1998, UnitedHealth Group acquired HealthPartners of Arizona, operator of Arizona's largest [AHCCCS](/wiki/Arizona_Health_Care_Cost_Containment_System "Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System") provider.[[21]](#cite_note-21)

After Liu Zhenya's retirement from State Grid, in 2016 [Shu Yinbiao](/wiki/Shu_Yinbiao "Shu Yinbiao") became the enterprise's Chairman and Party Secretary.[[5]](#cite_note-:Leutert-5): 97 Shu continued Liu's strategy of "one special, four large" and instituted a new strategy of "re-electrification" which sought to replace coal and petroleum power with electricity generated from renewable energy sources.[[5]](#cite_note-:Leutert-5): 98

As of 2024, SGCC is the world's largest energy utility company.[[15]](#cite_note-:Curtis&Klaus-15): 92 SGCC is the third biggest company in the world (as measured by revenues) in the 2023 [Fortune Global 500](/wiki/Fortune_Global_500 "Fortune Global 500").[[5]](#cite_note-:Leutert-5): 92 It operates almost all of China's energy transmission network.[[15]](#cite_note-:Curtis&Klaus-15): 92
